question: Should the lease-freshness checker guarantee that its own process returns after the deadline even if Git is uninterruptibly blocked by filesystem I/O, or is best-effort cancellation of killable Git hangs the intended contract?
rationale: A true return-time bound requires changing the synchronous execution/lifecycle model and deciding how to handle a child that cannot be killed immediately; that operator and cleanup tradeoff is not safely inferred from a two-line timeout addition.

options.title: Require a true caller deadline
options.body: Adopt a supervised execution model that lets the checker return at the deadline and explicitly defines descendant cleanup and observability.

options.title: Accept best-effort cancellation
options.body: Keep the synchronous helper but narrow the PR claim and documentation to killable Git hangs rather than stale-NFS hard-bound behavior.

recommendation.title: Require a true caller deadline
recommendation.body: Adopt a supervised execution model that lets the checker return at the deadline and explicitly defines descendant cleanup and observability.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available contributor with directly adjacent bounded-Git work, though a repository owner should make the contract decision.
